column1: # confusables_attested.tsv — real-attacker confusable mappings NOT in TR39 (#597).
# TR39 lists pairs that are *visually* confusable. Miss-mining the BitCore subset of
# the BitAbuse corpus (Lee et al., NAACL Findings 2025) with `benchmarks/adversarial_eval`
# surfaced codepoints that real attackers substitute for basic-Latin letters and that
# TR39 does not list as SOURCES at all, so normalize_confusables() left them unfolded.
# Why a separate file from confusables_supplement.tsv: that file declares itself
# "cross-script confusable mappings NOT in TR39" and pins its provenance to one measured
# dataset at a stated threshold (confusable-vision, danger >= 0.97, the OQ3 decision on
# #336). 18 of the sources here are Latin folding to Latin, and none comes from that
# dataset. Two admission criteria, two provenance stories, two files.
# Provenance: attestation in the BitAbuse *BitCore* subset (real attacker text), with the
# intended letter recovered by positional alignment against ground truth. Occurrence and
# row counts are per-codepoint BitCore figures from the #597 mining run (disarm 0.12.0,
# full 325,580-row corpus). The synthetic BitViper tail — 254 further codepoints,
# 733,029 occurrences — is EXCLUDED by construction, per the #39/#40 guardrail that these
# corpora are measuring instruments, never optimization targets. No row here is justified
# by a benchmark score.
# CONTRACT NOTE. Tier 1 rows are optical: genuine shape-twins of a Latin letter. Tier 2a
# rows are POSITIONAL — an attacker reached for an Armenian/Georgian/runic glyph by
# position in the word, not because it looks like the letter. Admitting them widens this
# table's contract from "visual confusable" to "observed attacker substitution". That is a
# deliberate decision recorded on #597; Unicode would not accept the 2a rows upstream.
# EXCLUDED. U+00DF ß was proposed as tier 2b (#597) and is deliberately NOT here.
# It is ordinary German orthography, and folding it to `b` turns "Müller Straße" into
# "Müller Strabe" — caught by tests/test_accented_latin_fidelity.py. Same class as the
# Romanian ț that #593 guards: a live letter in a major language is not a confusable
# source, however much it resembles one. Note the asymmetry this leaves — ẞ, ꞵ and Ꟗ fold
# through ß as their TR39 prototype (#595) while ß itself does not. That is intended: the
# prototype is a fold TARGET there, not a source.
# CASE NOTE. Six rows fold an uppercase source to a lowercase target (Ƿ Ʌ Ա Ⴝ Ⴍ Ⴓ),
# which no generated row does — the generated pipeline reconciles case to the source via
# fix_case_mismatch, and rows in this file bypass it. The attested form is kept, because
# the evidence is the letter the attacker meant, not its case.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   source   hex codepoint of the attested source character
#   latin    latin-target fold ("-" = no latin override; keep the generated value)
#   cyrillic cyrillic-target fold ("-" = no cyrillic override; SEVEN of these sources
#            already have a generated cyrillic mapping, which must not be disturbed)
#   tier     1 = optical · 2a = positional · 2b = convention
#   occ      BitCore occurrences (informative; never an admission criterion on its own)
#   note     glyph, Unicode name, and the intended letter
# source
